principle: Change WHAT BECOMES OPERATIVE TEXT. Do NOT change structuralNodeIds itself. Keeping the array intact is what makes every coverage / provenance / supersession consumer bit-identical (06-consumer-matrix.json C2, C5-C12).

changes.proposed:
const anchorNodeId = candidate.structuralNodeIds[0] ?? null;
const operativeSourceText = anchorNodeId ? index.getNodeText(anchorNodeId, "DESCENDANTS") : "";
changes.why: The one site that turns Pass C's LINK into a span. Everything else in this design follows from it.
risks: A candidate with an empty structuralNodeIds array yields "" - exactly what the current expression already yields for that case (an empty map joins to ""), so no new failure mode.
The compile cache key changes for every affected candidate (cache.ts:34): a one-time cold cache, no correctness effect.

changes.proposed: the same anchor-only expression as R1
changes.why: The pilot harness reproduces R1 byte-for-byte and is what every Phase-3 measurement runs through. Without it the validation would measure the old contract. Harness file - it does not count toward PRODUCTION_FILES_CHANGED, but it is REQUIRED for the change to be observable.

Gate 2 is the ONLY gate that can permit a review skip. Anchor-only operative text removes chapeau conditions from its window, so without this the fix could REDUCE review on exactly the composite cases the 14 false-credit controls protect.
risks: A mean 319 extra chars (max 758) on that one classifier input. No new call, no new model.

changes.current: for (const extraNodeId of candidate.structuralNodeIds.slice(1)) retrieveOperativeSource(state, access.index, documentId, extraNodeId);
changes.proposed: retrieve the linked node as a typed PARENT_SCOPE item (or SIBLING_CONTEXT when it is not an ancestor) rather than a second OPERATIVE_SOURCE item.
changes.why: After R1 this is the last place a linked parent's full subtree is still LABELLED operative. Measured: retrieveParentScope already emits the same parent as PARENT_SCOPE for 67/67 dual CONMED candidates, so the item is redundant as well as mislabelled. Deliberately NOT bundled with R1: leaving it keeps the first change strictly context-preserving - nothing a compiler sees today disappears - which is the property the paid validation should test first.

changes.proposed: add optional `role?: "OPERATIVE" | "CONTEXTUAL"` and optional `contextItemId?: string`; absent reads as OPERATIVE, so every existing IR artifact stays valid.
changes.why: Makes a contextual citation auditable. Not required for the span fix to be safe, because after R1 the operative window no longer contains the foreign text.

changes.proposed: an invariant test asserting that coverage-audit's discoveredNodeIds set and semantic-coverage's covered-unit set are identical before and after R1.
changes.why: Mechanically pins the 'coverage cannot disappear' claim instead of relying on the argument.

changes.proposed: reword the field's doc comment from 'nodes this discovery's evidence spans' to 'anchor node, followed by linked nodes that contextualise it'.
changes.why: The wording is what invited the defect. No behaviour change.

changes.proposed: emit the linkage as a separate named field (e.g. contextualNodeIds) instead of position [1..] of structuralNodeIds.
changes.why: Structurally clearer, but it touches every consumer in the matrix and turns a 2-line change into a migration. NOT recommended for this remediation.

notChanged: the compiler prompt or few-shots (the operative/context split already exists at caller.ts:229-244)
